title: Program wire — driver-semantics scenario (§10.3)
description: The two authored documents of a driver-semantics scenario: the event script and the per-step trace. The third file, the starting tree, is a REFERENCED document (§3) owned by the tree wire specification and is not described here. Like every schema in this directory these definitions are SUBORDINATE to PROGRAM_WIRE.md, and the gap is unusually wide for this family: a schema cannot say that a trace carries one entry per event PLUS the state before any of them, that the tree at a step is compared semantically while the effects beside it are compared byte-for-byte, or that a harness must report the FIRST divergent step. All three are in §10.3, and `wire-fixtures/check-scenarios.mjs` is what enforces them.

events.description: The ordered event script. Order is the drive order, and it is what the trace's step indices count.

nodeId.description: The originating node, threaded to the evaluator exactly as every placement threads it (§8.3).

event.description: The event name the surface would have delivered.

payload.description: The event's values, as a flat object of strings. Present even when empty: an omitted payload and an empty one would be two spellings of one fact.

trace.description: One entry per step. INDEX 0 IS THE STATE BEFORE ANY EVENT, so a trace is one longer than the script that drove it — an arithmetic relation between two files, which no schema can express and which §10.3 states and the corpus checker enforces.

denial.description: A denial (§5.3) as it appears in a step trace. Unlike the outcome document's position, `origin` IS reachable here: the client-effect arms name destinations, and a host declining one for its destination records which. A schema cannot say that `origin` may appear only on `GateRefused` — that is in §5.3, and `wire-fixtures/check-scenarios.mjs` enforces it — nor that a harness must DECODE these rather than diff their bytes, which is in §10.3.

origin.description: The destination the refusal was about — a network destination's HOST, or the class of destination where there is no host. Never the scheme, port, path or query: a denial record outlives its session, and the query string of a refused exfiltration attempt IS the payload.

tree.description: The resolved tree at this step, EMBEDDED AS A DOCUMENT rather than as a string of one implementation's bytes. That is what makes the expectation placement-independent: a host decodes it with its own decoder and compares against its own resolved tree, so a host whose encoder differs from the one that generated the scenario is not held to bytes this specification does not own (§3).

effects.description: The client effects (§5.2) this step emitted, in order. Each is a STRING whose contents are the effect document's own bytes — recorded as emitted, never as an embedded object, because embedding one would licence a JSON writer to re-order its members Ordinally and so erase the specification's one enumerated envelope exception in the one place nobody would notice.

refused.description: Whether the loop refused the event that produced this step. Always false at index 0, where no event has yet been delivered.

denials.description: OPTIONAL. The effects this host's performer seam declined at this step, in order, embedded as documents. Its ABSENCE means none-or-unobserved and is not a claim that nothing was declined; an EMPTY array is the positive claim that the seam was consulted and declined nothing. A host whose scenario runner consults no seam omits the member rather than writing an empty array — the two spellings carry different facts here, which is the opposite of the rule everywhere else in this specification and is why §10.3 states it. A step that emitted nothing can have declined nothing, so index 0 never carries a non-empty array.
